judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's content claims all hold. I rendered every page and re-derived the figures from worksheet.tex: problem 1 is a rectangle in four equal parts, problem 2 a circle in three equal slices, problem 4's bar A is six equal pieces against bar B's six unequal ones, problem 5's detached strip is drawn 0.52 cm wide against a 2.67 cm bar of five parts (exactly one fifth), problem 6's two rectangles are identical (both 276-489 px wide in a 90 dpi render) cut into 3 and 6, and problem 7's three squares are all 1.7 cm on a side cut into 2, 8 and 4 — so the ordering 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 really is B, C, A. The judge's manual review of item 8 is also correct and the item is properly typed {"type": "manual"}. But two things escaped the judge, one of them a confirmed instance of a known systemic defect. First, answer_key_quality cannot be 4/4: problem 6 is a VERIFIED compare entry ({"type": "compare", "values": ["1/3", "1/6"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"}) and the Quick Answers bank prints '6. —' for it, the same em-dash printed at '8. —' for the genuinely manual item. Two rows apart, a grader cannot tell a machine-proved answer from one nobody checked. I confirmed the mechanism: render_quick_answers._fmt calls sympy.sympify('>'), which raises SympifyError, and the except branch returns '---', the glyph render_entry also returns for manual-only ids. Second, problem 4 asks the child to 'draw a big X on the bar whose shaded piece cannot be named that way' — a marked response — and verify.json id 4 records only the eval 1/6, with no manual companion. Third, and separately from the judge: problem 3's stem and the key both call the figure a 'square' when worksheet.tex lines 51-57 draw a 5.6 cm by 2.8 cm rectangle.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is correctly typed {"type": "manual"} and its desc carries a usable rubric rather than a placeholder ('a shape is cut into 3 pieces that are not the same size and a classmate calls the shaded piece one third. The child must explain why the name does not fit'), so the single open item on the sheet is honestly declared and the build exits with a manual flag.

The comparison figures are drawn to genuinely congruent wholes, which is the whole basis of unit-fraction comparison: I measured problem 6's two rectangles as identical and problem 7's three squares as 1.7 cm on every side, so a child who reasons from the picture reaches the right order rather than being rescued by the caption.

Problem 5 isolates the misconception that actually causes unit-fraction errors — a part physically drawn away from its whole — and declares the trap as a/(b-1), the 'count what is left in the bar' error, with the key naming it: 'the bottom number counts how many equal parts the whole was cut into, and that number never changes when a piece is moved.'

Problem 4 makes 'are the parts equal?' a prerequisite question rather than an afterthought by printing a fair and an unfair six-part bar side by side, and the key states the idea the whole sheet rests on: 'bar B still shows a shaded piece of a whole — it is just not one sixth, because sixths have to be the same size.'

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expecteds with bare sympy.sympify, and a relation operator is not a sympifiable expression, so the fallback prints '---'. The same glyph is what render_entry returns for a manual-only id, so the bank collapses 'verified relation' and 'nobody checked this' into one symbol. This is the canonical quick-answer-bank-drops-relation-answers defect, confirmed here on a second case.
evidence: verify.json id 6: {"type": "compare", "values": ["1/3", "1/6"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"} — a machine-verified answer, and gate_log.txt records verify-ws PASS.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '6. —' and '8. —' in the same block; id 8 is the sheet's only {"type": "manual"} entry.

scripts/render_quick_answers.py line 57-61: the str branch returns '"$" + sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)) + "$"' and falls back to '---' on SympifyError; line 71-74: render_entry returns '---' when a problem has no expected at all.
Reproduced directly: sympy.sympify('>') raises SympifyError, as does '<' and '=', while '1/8' sympifies fine — which is why problem 7's ordered list prints correctly and problem 6 does not.
The answer key body has the value all along: problem 6 step 3 prints 'The third is bigger, so 1/3 > 1/6.' Only the bank loses it.

root_causes.description: An item requiring the student to MARK the page (draw an X on the unfair bar) is recorded as an ordinary machine-verified eval covering only the item's numeric half, with no manual companion, so the marked half of the response is neither checked nor declared as needing a human read.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'Write the fraction for the shaded piece of the bar that has equal pieces. Then draw a big X on the bar whose shaded piece cannot be named that way.'
verify.json id 4: one entry, {"type": "eval", "expr": "a/b", "at": {"a": 1, "b": 6}, "expected": "1/6"} — nothing records which bar should carry the X.
The answer key does supply it in prose ('Only bar A is cut into equal parts ... Bar B gets the X'), so the grader is served; the verification record is not.

root_causes.description: The figure for problem 3 is a 2:1 rectangle but the worksheet stem and the answer key both name it a square. In a band whose geometry strand is about classifying shapes by attributes, printing the wrong shape name on a figure the child is told to look at teaches the opposite of that strand.
evidence: worksheet.tex lines 51-57: '\draw[thick] (0,0) rectangle (5.6,2.8)' with three vertical cuts at 1.4, 2.8, 4.2 and one horizontal at 1.4 — an outer rectangle 5.6 cm by 2.8 cm, twice as wide as it is tall (confirmed in the 90 dpi render: 199 px by 103 px).
worksheet.pdf problem 3: 'Count the equal parts in this square — count the parts, not the lines that make them.'

answer_key.pdf problem 3 heading: 'Square cut into eight equal parts', and step 1: 'The square is cut by three up-and-down lines and one across, and all the small rectangles that result are the same size.' The eight PARTS are 1.4 cm squares; the whole is not.
The same sheet's problem 7 correctly calls three 1.7 cm figures 'squares', so the vocabulary is right elsewhere in the document.

improvements.title: Render verified compare relations in the Quick Answers bank instead of the manual em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation expecteds before the sympify attempt: map the operator set {'<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!='} to their LaTeX forms ($<$, $>$, $=$, $\le$, $\ge$, $\ne$) and return them directly. For an 'order': 'relation' compare entry, prefer printing the full statement built from the entry's own 'values' — '$\frac{1}{3} > \frac{1}{6}$' rather than a bare operator — since a lone '>' in a bank is nearly as unhelpful as a dash. Independently, reserve '---' for genuinely unchecked items: give render_entry a distinct marker for manual ids (for example the existing dash plus a footnoted 'manual'), so the bank never prints the same glyph for a proved answer and an unproved one. Fix alongside quick-answers-must-not-typeset-python-builtins, which shares the bare-sympify mechanism but needs the opposite remedy.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py assert that render_entry([{"type": "compare", "values": ["1/3", "1/6"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"}]) returns a string containing '>' (and the two fractions) and NOT equal to '---', and that render_entry([{"type": "manual", "desc": "..."}]) still returns the manual marker — the two must differ. The first assertion fails today because sympify('>') raises and the except branch returns '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Every verified relation across the run becomes readable in the bank, and the bank regains its one job: telling a grader at a glance which items were proved. On this sheet, '6. —' becomes '6. 1/3 > 1/6' and '8. —' stays the honest manual marker.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is additive inside one formatting function. The one thing to watch is LaTeX math-mode escaping of the operators inside the bank's multicol environment — the existing '$...$' wrapping already used for sympified output covers it, and the render-quick-answers gate compiles the bank, so a mistake fails the build rather than shipping.

improvements.title: Require a manual companion entry for items that ask the student to mark or draw on the page
improvements.proposed_change: Add the open-response stem scan to tests/check_answer_line.py, matching drawing and marking imperatives ('draw', 'sketch', 'circle', 'cross', 'mark', 'shade', 'X on') as well as explanation verbs, and exit 1 when the matching id carries no {"type": "manual"} entry. For curr-081, id 4 keeps its 1/6 eval and gains a manual entry recording what the mark must be — 'the X belongs on bar B, whose six pieces are unequal' — which is exactly the sentence the answer key already prints.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/fixtures/marked_response_unflagged/ with a worksheet problem reading 'Write the fraction for the shaded piece of the bar that has equal pieces. Then draw a big X on the bar whose shaded piece cannot be named that way.' and a verify.json id 1 holding only the eval for 1/6. Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 naming problem 1 and 'draw'; add the manual entry and assert exit 0.
improvements.expected_impact: The marked half of a two-part item is declared rather than implied. Here it also improves the delivery text, which currently reports one manual item where there are two responses a human must look at.
improvements.risk: 'circle' and 'draw' appear innocently in geometry prose ('draw a circle around the centre point'), so the scan must run on stem text only and the message must make the one-line fix obvious.

improvements.title: Name a figure by what the TikZ actually draws — problem 3 calls a 2:1 rectangle a square
improvements.proposed_change: Reword problem 3's stem and the matching answer-key heading to 'this rectangle' (the eight parts are squares; the whole is not), or redraw the outer shape as a genuine square — for example a 2.8 cm by 2.8 cm square cut into eight equal 1.4 by 0.7 cm parts — if a square whole is wanted. Add a line to references/problem-library.md's figure guidance stating that the shape noun in a stem is a mathematical claim in bands where shape classification is in scope, and must be checked against the drawn coordinates, not against the author's mental picture. A cheap mechanical guard is possible for the common cases: when a stem's shape noun is 'square' and the region's TikZ contains a single '\draw ... rectangle (w,h)' with w != h, fail.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/fixtures/shape_name_mismatch/ containing a worksheet problem whose stem says 'Count the equal parts in this square' over a TikZ region drawing '\draw[thick] (0,0) rectangle (5.6,2.8)'. Assert the new shape-noun check exits 1 naming problem 1, the noun 'square' and the drawn dimensions 5.6 x 2.8; change the coordinates to (2.8,2.8) and assert exit 0.
improvements.expected_impact: Stops a fractions sheet from teaching wrong shape vocabulary to the same graders and children who will meet 3.G.A classification a few weeks later. One-word fix on this sheet; the guard prevents the class of error.
improvements.risk: A regex over shape nouns and TikZ coordinates will not generalise past axis-aligned rectangles, and it will not see shapes drawn as coordinate paths (which is how curr-098 draws its quadrilaterals). Ship it as a narrow, high-precision check rather than a general shape verifier, and keep the reference-material guidance as the broader remedy.

case_summary: Visually the best-built sheet in this batch: I measured the rendered figures and the comparison wholes are genuinely congruent (problem 6's two rectangles identical, problem 7's three squares all 1.7 cm), problem 5's detached strip is drawn at exactly one fifth of its bar, and problem 4's fair and unfair six-part bars make 'equal parts first' a prerequisite rather than a footnote. Item 8 is correctly declared manual with a real rubric. Three defects sit under the 32/32. The most consequential is a confirmed instance of a known systemic renderer bug: problem 6 is a VERIFIED compare (expected '>') and the Quick Answers bank prints '6. —', the identical glyph printed at '8. —' for the genuinely manual item, because render_quick_answers._fmt hands '>' to bare sympy.sympify, which raises, and the fallback returns the manual dash. The bank's only job is telling a grader what was proved, and on this sheet it says the opposite. Second, problem 4 asks the child to draw an X on the unfair bar and nothing in verify.json records the marked half of the response. Third, problem 3's stem and key call a 5.6 by 2.8 cm rectangle a 'square' — the eight parts are squares, the whole is not — in a grade band whose geometry strand is shape classification. None of these change a computed fraction; all three are fixable without touching a number.
